Carrie Eglinton Manner: Yes. Part of the reason we shared more of the Ebola background is that major catalyst that I talked about, the BRIDGE Access Study, obviously, we were hoping that you have seen the results of that sooner. That study was announced in May. Inclusion in that was in June. The descriptions of it were moving at the speed of the outbreak. And considering that this is the fastest-growing outbreak to date, the need for diagnostics and rapid testing is so clear that I think everybody is expecting that to be a major catalyst to drive that contracting. So quite frankly, I would have expected that already. We are not unusual in waiting for this.

I mean I know the U.S. government is -- we work with BARDA and CDC, and we're all waiting on that as a catalyst to sort of open up the regional ordering. What I would say is that like we've emphasized, we've got decades-long relationships. We will serve needs that are already contracting. But this is a matter of new processes in place that were not sort of well defined. But fundamentally, we feel very well positioned to work with these partners who we support, who we partner with today. And we've been very encouraged. They've been figuring out funding and implementation paths for all of the rest of their diagnostic needs.

We believe that, that will be the case with Ebola as well. And there are really strong partnerships that we plan to continue to build on. So while we don't know the timing precisely, we do expect that before the end of the year. And as soon as we know more, we'll be sharing that.

Operator: I'm showing no further questions. I'd like to turn the call back over to Carrie Eglinton Manner for any closing remarks.

Carrie Eglinton Manner: Thank you. Thank you for your interest and participating in our call. We look forward to our offline discussions as well as following up next quarter. Thanks so much. With that, we'll close.

#3061. Lakers’ bench comes up big in road win over Hawks

For the second night in a row, the Lakers picked up a tough road win while shorthanded, this time beating the Hawks 124-114 on Monday to extend their winning streak to six games.

Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (right finger sprain) were both out for the game, placing a heavier burden on the Lakers' role players to step up. The response came in the form of a season-high 49 bench points.

LA scored 29 points off 20 Hawks turnovers and, again, won the points in the paint battle, 52-42.

The Hawks grabbed the lead and momentum early in the first period. Onyeka Okongwu led them with seven points. LA was 3-7 from the field. Ziaire Williams got the Lakers' first basket in a triple. Luka Dončić made his first shot attempt, but had three of the team's turnovers.

At the 6:53 mark, the Hawks were up eight.

Luka inched closer to his usual double figures in the first quarter, pushing his total to seven. With Austin Reaves out, Cameron Carr saw minutes in the rotation. He had two rebounds.

The first ended with back-to-back dunks from Carr and Jarred Vanderbilt, both assisted by Luka, and a triple from Sandro Mamukelashvili. LA was up by nine.

Los Angeles was cooking early in the second period with Williams and Mamu both knocking down triples. Collin Sexton also connected with Walker Kessler twice for dunks.

LA was on an extended 28-9 scoring run. Every Laker off the bench, minus Adou Theiro, had scored.

Sexton continued to give the purple and gold a huge boost. He now had nine points with four assists. He and Kessler helped give Los Angeles a 19-point lead with 6:34 left.

CJ McCollum and Nickeil Alexander-Walker brought some life to the Hawks, combining for 12 points to shave points off the lead. After being down by as much as 20, Atlanta crawled back on the shoulders of Jalen Johnson to cut the deficit to 11 at halftime.

Williams began the third period with the first four points. Atlanta, though, still had momentum and were still slowly chipping away at LA's lead. They got within six, with Dyson Daniels heating up and scoring five points.

Both teams turned on the offensive jets, scoring at a ridiculous high level.

Alexander-Walker got hot for Atlanta, scoring nine points. Luka and Mamu combined for 11 points. Los Angeles was shooting 46% from the field and the Hawks were close behind with 44%

The Lakers let Atlanta gain steam again as they knocked down three triples. They got to within three, but Luka converted on a midrange jumper, giving LA a five-point lead at the end of the third.

Mamu continued his stellar play by knocking down a 3-pointer to start the final frame. He had an impressive 19 points off the bench. The Hawks cut the deficit all the way down to two thanks to Aaron Wiggins scoring five points.

Los Angeles answered immediately with four straight points to take a six-point lead with 8:22 left.

The three ball was proving to be important for both teams as the Lakers saw Sexton make another, but Aaron Wiggins and McCollum drained two for the Hawks, getting the team to within four with 4:29 left.

Los Angeles erupted for a wonderful 9-2 scoring run on the shoulders of Mamu, Luka, Williams, LaRavia and Matisse Thybulle, putting the finishing touches on a great performance.

Luka finished with 32 points, eight rebounds, 10 assists and five steals. Kessler ended with 21 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Sexton had 18 points and six assists off the bench.

Mamu logged 23 points with eight rebounds and three assists. Williams pitched in with 12 points. Thybulle had six points, all of which came at moments the team needed big shots.

Carr ended with two points and three rebounds. Thiero had two rebounds, an assist and a steal.

The Lakers' next game will be against the Atlanta Hawks on Monday at 4:00 PM PT.

You can follow Karin on Twitter at @KarinAbcarians.

#3060. AppLovin: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

AppLovin's architecture overhaul is still in progress, so the payoff from the new AI models remains unproven for long-term holders.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 4, 2026, AppLovin (APP +4.80%) announced that revenue jumped 55% year over year to $2.18 billion. The company is generating massive cash flow while expanding its ad engine beyond mobile gaming into broad e-commerce categories. Three things management said stand out.

Engineers began rolling out a structural architectural update to Axon, the deep learning algorithm that predicts user actions and matches ads to mobile app users. Early performance metrics show advertisers spent more money profitably, particularly in newer non-gaming consumer categories where historical data is sparse.

Mobile gaming has traditionally generated most of the business, but non-gaming e-commerce brands are rapidly ramping up spend on the platform. Management sees this consumer vertical providing an extended runway as new advertisers validate performance through return on ad spend, a metric that measures ad revenue against ad spend.

AppLovin converted roughly 65% of its top line into free cash flow this quarter, giving management the firepower to repurchase $1.4 billion of stock. Retiring shares at this pace amplifies per-share returns while net leverage, which measures debt relative to adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, remains near zero.

Ad spend is surging across mobile games and e-commerce, and leadership is signaling total comfort with its compounding trajectory. The company maintains an asset-light model, high profit-to-cash conversion, and expanding ad inventory on connected television, which serves streaming video ads to smart televisions.

Management is focusing near-term execution on finishing the architecture transition, attracting new e-commerce advertisers, and scaling connected television campaigns.

#3057. Via: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Over 95% of Via's code is now written with AI, a productivity gain that may matter more to margins than to new contracts.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 9, 2026, Via (VIA +12.80%) announced revenue grew 31% year over year to $144 million as customer contracts expanded. Broadening software adoption across municipal transit agencies and disciplined spending are moving the transit technology provider toward net profitability. Three takeaways from management's comments illustrate how the business is evolving.

When Via manages an entire transit network, it replaces pen-and-paper systems with software across fleet scheduling, maintenance, and dispatching. These end-to-end contracts yield immediate efficiency gains for transit agencies, so Via doesn't have to rebuild its sales effort for every new city.

Rising fuel prices and vehicle ownership costs are pushing commuters toward public transportation. U.S. voters recently approved ballot initiatives that will generate $30 billion in local funding. That unlocks fresh expansion opportunities for Via's transit software.

Automated engineering and customer support tools are lowering internal operating expenses across the business. Software automation helped raise adjusted gross margin to 40.5%. The company doesn't need to bloat headcount to ship new features faster.

Revenue expanded 31% year over year in the third quarter while operating expenses grew at a much slower rate. Regional customer density creates flywheel effects that lower sales costs in neighboring cities, while internal software automation accelerates product delivery. Management is tracking sales pipeline conversion and gross margin consistency.

Expanding into school transportation extends Via's core platform into adjacent municipal markets. Converting a record pipeline while locking in profitability defines the primary operational focus heading into next year.

#3053. IonQ Shares Surge as Revenue Soars. Is It Too Late to Buy the Quantum Computing Stock?

IonQ shares jumped after the company's revenue came in well above expectations.

While an investment in IonQ (IONQ +8.34%) is largely about the long-term future of quantum computing and its potential to become one of the top companies in this nascent field, the company is starting to deliver impressive revenue and growth right now.

IonQ has proven to be one of the early leaders in quantum computing, with its trapped-ion technology supplemented by microwave antennas embedded directly into its chips, achieving the highest fidelity (accuracy) in the space at 99.99%.

Meanwhile, it recently made a breakthrough in quantum error correction (QEC), developing an end-to-end real-time QEC decoder using an off-the-shelf central processing unit (CPU). At the same time, the quantum computing company has been aggressively making acquisitions in the quantum space, as it looks to take a page from Nvidia's book and become a complete ecosystem player.

Let's take a closer look at the company's Q3 earnings report and prospects to see whether the stock's rally can continue or if it's too late to buy.

The past few months have been important for IonQ. It closed its acquisition of quantum foundry SkyWater at the end of July, advanced to Stage 3 of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's (DARPA) Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, and acquired zero-trust network security company Elisity to bolster its cybersecurity capabilities.

In the third quarter, IonQ's revenue soared 336% to $173.8 million from $39.9 million a year ago. That was well above the $141.6 million analyst consensus.

IonQ platform revenue jumped 127% to $90.3 million, powered by deployments of its Tempo systems and sensing products. SkyWater, meanwhile, contributed $83.5 million in sales from its two months under IonQ. It said SkyWater's revenue growth was strong, as it added new customers and expanded existing relationships.

About 65% of its revenue came from commercial customers as they began using its solutions for real-world purposes. Meanwhile, 35% of revenue came from international markets, while 40% came from multi-product sales.

Remaining performance obligations (RPOs), which can be an indicator of future growth, came in at $1.2 billion, with $479 million from SkyWater. IonQ platform RPO jumped 42% sequentially to $689 million. The company signed $290 million worth of contracts in the quarter, including $180 million for quantum computing systems.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) came in at a loss of $133.68 million, compared to a loss of $48.9 million a year ago. Adjusted EPS, meanwhile, was a loss of $0.29 versus a loss of $0.17 a year ago. However, that topped the analyst consensus for a $0.38 loss.

IonQ also continues to burn cash, with negative operating cash flow of $570.3 million over the past nine months, and negative free cash flow of $605.2 million. It currently has around $3.7 billion in cash and investments on its balance sheet and minimal debt, after a $2 billion equity offering in October after the quarter.

The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $505 million to $515 million, up from a prior outlook of $280 million to $290 million before the SkyWater acquisition was completed. It now expects quantum computing growth of 110%, up from a prior outlook of 100%. Meanwhile, it is sold out of capacity for its new sixth-generation Superion 256 systems for 2027.

IonQ has become a clear leader in the quantum computing space, and this is starting to show up in real revenue. The company has one of the most accurate systems, which positions it well to eventually create a fault-tolerant system.

That said, with quantum computing stocks, I'd still prefer a basket approach that includes multiple stocks, as betting on a single technology and company at this stage carries significant risk. While IonQ's systems lead in accuracy, they're not as strong in QEC as some other players, and the trapped-ion technique is not as fast as other approaches, such as superconducting qubits. Nonetheless, given the company's strengths, this is definitely a top quantum stock to own; it just wouldn't be my only bet on the future of quantum technology.

Geoffrey Seiler has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends IonQ and Nvidia. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

#3052. Warriors have no urgency to trade Porzingis, give up draft picks

The Golden State Warriors would like to trade Kristaps Porzingis by December 15. However, they're not about to sacrifice draft capital to do it for a long-term contract.

There's not a ton of pressure on the Warriors to trade Porzingis, who isn't being paid as he decides to "step away" from basketball, which he allegedly loves. He and the NBA Players Association aren't planning to challenge to Warriors taking him off the payroll, which saves Joe Lacob about $250K per game. He may not play this season, for the Warriors or anyone else, but that doesn't mean his contract is an albatross.

According to Clutch Points, the Warriors have had trade talks regarding Porzingis with the Chicago Bulls, New Orleans Pelicans, and Milwaukee Bucks. They're reportedly interested in 26-year-old center Jalen Smith of the Bulls, who is making $9.4M in the last year of his contract. It's not clear who on the Pelicans' roster has interested the Warriors, but with the Bucks, it's center Myles Turner, who is signed through 2029 for $82.6M.

The Bucks want the Warriors to give them draft picks in a Turner trade, which would have to include another player (Moses Moody?) heading to Milwaukee, as the Warriors can't take back more money than they send out. The Warriors think that taking on that much of Turner's salary means they should be getting a draft pick, not the Bucks.

Turner is having a wretched season for the Bucks, who are in a weird rebuild limbo since trading Giannis Antetokounmpo this summer. They got four players back from the Miami Heat, drafted two players in the lottery, and have veterans Tyler Herro, Kyle Kuzma, and Caris Levert on expiring deals. They're 1-9 and since they don't have their own first-round pick until 2031, the Bucks don't even have incentive to avoid the lottery penalty for having one of the league's worst records.

The 30-year-old Turner is averaging 7.1 points and 5.7 rebounds this season, though he is blocking 2.5 shots per game. His effort seems to be lacking, as seen in a blowout loss to the Boston Celtics Sunday.

What Turner can provide, assuming he's trying, is a rare combination of rim protection and outside shooting. He's a career 36.4% three-point shooter and has blocked 2.1 shots per game for his career. Turner was the pivot man on an Indiana Pacers team that was a Tyrese Haliburton Achilles injury from winning a title. It's easy to see how he's a logical replacement for Porzingis, with the bonus that he's played at least 71 games the last three seasons.

But his contract is n0t good. It's even worse for the Bucks, since they waived-and-stretched Damian Lillard's contract to afford the deal, and Dame Time now costs them $22.5M on the salary cap for each of the next four seasons. By contrast, Porzingis is on the books for only $3M next season, isn't get paid anything right now, and might take a buyout on the $17M+ remaining on this year's deal.

The key calendar date for the Warriors is Dec. 15, because of the NBA's "reaggregation" rule. Players acquired before that date can be combined with other players/contracts until the trade deadline. This came up for the Warriors in Dec. 2024, when they traded De'Anthony Melton for Dennis Schroder just before the reaggregation deadline, then aggregated Schroder's salary in the blockbuster trade for Jimmy Butler.

That's why a player like Smith could be more appealing for the Warriors than Smith, as he could provide temporary help while still remaining highly moveable in a later trade. The Warriors could conceivably take back their old friend Buddy Hield in such a trade, as his salary and Smith's are still less than Porzingis' total money — and Hield can be waived next summer for just over $3M.

There's a lot of possibilities for what the Warriors do with Porzingis. But giving up future draft picks to ditch him does not seem to be one of them.

#3049. Micron Is Down 40% Since Oct. 7. History Suggests a $5,000 Investment Today Could Be Worth This Much by 2030.

Is the memory giant's crash a buying opportunity?

The last month hasn't been kind to Micron Technology (MU +6.25%) shareholders. The memory-chip maker's stock price fell by 40% over the 29 days from Oct. 7 to the close on Nov. 5. The company is particularly susceptible to shifts in supply and demand for memory, and various factors have impacted the outlook for both in recent weeks, much to the detriment of Micron's earnings potential.

But after that huge share price drop, investors may see an opportunity to put some extra cash to work in Micron stock. Here's what a $5,000 investment at today's price could be worth by 2030 based on its historical valuation range.

It's not just Micron stock under pressure. The entire semiconductor industry has seen valuations decline over the past month. That's largely due to concerns over the outlook for artificial intelligence spending. As hyperscalers report increasing cash burn while spending heavily on new data centers, some investors have expressed doubts that their returns on investment will be high enough to justify the costs. With the vast majority of Micron's growth stemming from the data center build-out, its stock has been pushed lower.

There are additional factors specific to Micron and other memory-chip makers, too. Chinese competitor CXMT is reportedly increasing production of its HBM3 chips, the type of memory that is packaged with GPUs and other AI accelerator chips. Apple is also reportedly testing CXMT chips in Chinese-manufactured iPhones.

Meanwhile, high memory chip prices and supply shortages have driven up prices for consumer electronics, pushing tech companies to scale back the amount of memory they are putting in their devices. That leaves memory-chip makers more dependent on demand from artificial intelligence. If that falters, their ability to fall back on the consumer electronics segment will be more precarious.

In the wake of the Democrats' strong showing in the midterm elections, there's growing fear that the AI industry could face setbacks due to a tougher regulatory environment. UBS analysts estimate 30% of data center capacity additions planned for 2028 are at risk of delays. That could put further pressure on demand for the chips those data centers would need, in turn weighing on the pricing for Micron's memory.

And Micron management has already indicated that pricing for memory is nearing its peak. Management's 2027 forecast calls for "a more moderate rate of price increases." Peak pricing could hit in early 2028, and an influx of new production capacity could push prices significantly lower in 2029 and 2030. If data center build-outs slow down, those price declines could come sooner and be much steeper.

After Micron's precipitous drop, shares trade for just 3.7 times analysts' forward earnings estimates. That's near the low end of its historic trading range, and the multiple it typically trades at right at the peak of its earnings cycle. The rapid price drop suggests the market is signaling that analysts' earnings growth estimates are too optimistic, that the company may be closer to peak earnings than previously thought, or both.

Micron's massive spending today will translate into significant depreciation expense on its income statement once it starts producing chips in its new facilities. Combined with rising operating expenses and the expected decline in pricing later this decade, Micron's margins are set to decline considerably from the inflated levels it has seen recently. That could lead to a long and protracted down cycle after the sharp up cycle it's experienced over the last few quarters. That could be another reason to keep the earnings multiple conservative.

While analysts expect earnings to peak at $227.1 billion in 2028, they project a slow decline in earnings through 2030, reaching just $148.7 billion. Earnings are expected to continue declining in 2031 at a much sharper rate, falling to $65.5 billion. That should give investors pause about Micron commanding a significantly high earnings multiple until it shows signs that earnings have reached a trough. A trailing earnings multiple between 5 and 10 isn't unreasonable, which would put Micron's market cap between $750 billion and $1.5 trillion if analysts' estimates are accurate.

That's a huge range, and depending on where it lands within it, a $5,000 investment at today's price could be worth about the same amount in four years, or it could double. There are significant risks facing the company, and they're starting to show up. Investors looking for returns like those Micron has produced over the past year are unlikely to see them, but after its recent decline in share price, there's less downside risk left.

#3043. Player Grades: Cavs vs Hornets – James Harden reaches DEFCON 1

The Cleveland Cavaliers lost to the Charlotte Hornets 124-112 in a game that trailed by as much as 30 points.

This is, without a doubt, one of the most alarming and concerning games the Cavs have played in the last five seasons.

Grades are based on our usual expectations for each player.

Thomas and the Cavs' youth were responsible for some of the only inspiring basketball that was played tonight.

They weren't perfect, but Thomas led the way with an energetic half that showed most of the team's issues are centered on not trying hard enough.

Thomas shot 7-12 from the floor. His effort and shot-making allowed the Cavs reserves to cut the deficit to within single digits.

Mitchell has cleaned up his offensive process in recent games to strike a solid balance between playmaking and scoring. His approach offensively wasn't the issue tonight. It was his defensive effort, and the fact that this team has lost all semblance of an identity around him.

Allen was awesome in the first quarter of this game. He made his return with a bang, detonating on a lob pass for the first play of the game. He finished the opening quarter with 9 points and 4 rebounds on a perfect 4-4 shooting. He even drilled a three-pointer.

It's not Allen's fault that everything went down the drain.

9 points, 2 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals, 1 block

Mobley is expected to be capable of transcending all of this. I can't give him a pass for fading into the background when the team is spiraling out of control. He's one of the players who is supposed to stabilize things. This wasn't it.

11 points, 5 assists, 3 rebounds, 4 turnovers

Harden has not looked good this season. Far from it. He's hit a new low defensively, and he's nowhere near good enough on offense right now to justify his minutes. This is a DEFCON 1 situation that can't be ignored.

The Cavs traded for Harden, and then extended him, understanding that the league has been rapidly moving away from his style of play. His slow-paced, heliocentric offense could only carry you so far even in his prime. At 37, Harden isn't showing that he'll be able to adapt his game to no longer being a one-man wrecking crew.

Watson has not been able to find his niche yet. Most of his scoring comes outside of the team's system — and he is not providing enough defensively to tip the scales.

Hezonja is hitting some speed bumps recently but is still someone who I'd feel comfortable giving more minutes to. He plays hard, and he probably has more offensive production in the tank if Cleveland can figure out where he fits.

I've given the Cavs flak for signing Bryant as soon as free agency began last summer. That's only because I think it was worth doing your due diligence and searching for a potential upgrade. It is not to disrespect or invalidate Bryant as a stone-cold veteran who plays every possession like it's life or death.

Bryant plays with a sense of urgency and is a fine role model for the younger players on this team.

Proctor was part of the inspiring group that brought this game back into reach. Effort and energy matter. Looking like you care about basketball matters. The intention that Proctor plays with on each possession was enough to string together stops and scores. Aka, winning basketball.

What a turn of events it's been for Minix. This wasn't a barn burner by any means; he shot just 1-of-4, but Minix deserves a ton of credit for brushing off the fact that this team waived him last week and only brought him back due to necessity. He's played hard and was a positive tonight, given the circumstances.

Omier is another two-way prospect who had a chance to get some run tonight. He made his impact through hustle, and as is the theme, that was enough to make him a positive in stark contrast to the starters.

Porter showed signs of life after a fairly troubling start to the season. He got downhill and looked effective as a ball-handler again. The Cavs would love it if he could get back to being a plus defender and creator.

#3038. No Austin Reaves, no problem. First-place Lakers beat Hawks for sixth consecutive win

Austin Reaves took the baton from Luka Doncic when Doncic sat out Sunday, and when the roles were reversed Monday, Doncic passed it to his teammates.

Doncic had 32 points and 10 assists in a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks as the Lakers relied on their depth to secure their sixth consecutive win and stay atop the Western Conference despite a short, tired bench.

One night after sitting out because of lower-back tightness, Doncic struggled with his shot but reached double-digit assists for the third time this season. He also had eight rebounds and five steals. Lakers center Walker Kessler had 21 points with 10 rebounds, his sixth double-double in seven games, and forward Sandro Mamukelashvili had what coach JJ Redick called "his best game as a Laker" with 23 points and eight rebounds off the bench to help overcome the absences of Reaves and Quentin Grimes.

Read more: Austin Reaves steps up in Luka Doncic's absence to lead Lakers over Pistons

Reaves, who scored 43 points in a thrilling win at Detroit on Sunday, didn't play because of illness. Grimes suffered a sprained finger on his right hand against Detroit, although Redick doesn't anticipate the injury keeping the guard sidelined for long. X-rays were negative, Redick said, and Grimes could return as soon as Wednesday in Milwaukee.

The Lakers (10-2) didn't look like a team playing on consecutive nights. They blitzed the Hawks (7-5) with 13 unanswered points at the end of the first quarter and ran the lead to 20 midway in the second quarter. Kessler and guard Collin Sexton connected on back-to-back alley-oops during the quarter to inject life into a shorthanded second unit.

"It's building resiliency," Kessler said. "JJ talks about it, going through adversity and understanding that to be a championship team, you've got to respond to that kind of stuff."

Reaves' absence was compounded by Grimes' injury, decimating the team's ballhandling unit. Redick and general manager Rob Pelinka had worked to stock the roster with guards to ward off the possibility of leaving too much responsibility to Doncic. On Monday, it all fell to Doncic and Sexton.

Lakers star Luka Doncic drives between Atlanta's Dyson Daniels, right, and Luguentz Dort in the first quarter Monday. (Kevin C. Cox / Getty Images)

Doncic, who came in averaging a league-high 40.1 points per game, leaned on teammates early with five assists in the first quarter. Sexton got going in the second quarter with eight points and three assists, all on lobs to Kessler, his former teammate with the Utah Jazz and fellow Atlanta native. Sexton finished with 18 points and six assists.

The 6-foot-1 guard signed during free agency when the Lakers wanted to stock the bench with play-making, shooting and defensive intensity. Sexton, playing on his fourth team in three seasons, has delivered on every one.

"He just checks a lot of boxes," Redick said. "For us, it was easy. He expressed interest, and obviously we wanted him, and it's worked out."

Sexton went to high school 15 miles from State Farm Arena. He estimated he had 400 to 500 people in the stands rooting for him. He stayed on the court for more than an hour after the game taking photos with the hundreds who waited.

In front of his city, Sexton wanted to win, no matter what his role would be within the Lakers' shorthanded rotation.

"Whenever those guys are in or out, I have to adjust," Sexton said. "And I feel like adjusting is something I've been doing my entire career."

The Lakers relied on their two youngest players for support. Second-year forward Adou Thiero, who made his season debut only two games ago after struggling with left knee swelling, had two points, two rebounds, an assist and a steal.

Rookie Cameron Carr earned his first rotation minutes and even started the fourth quarter. Carr, whose father, Chris, played in the NBA and famously lost the 1997 dunk contest to Kobe Bryant, scored his first NBA points, appropriately, on a dunk. Doncic snatched a pass from the Hawks and hit Carr on an outlet pass. The 21-year-old rookie gathered for an emphatic, two-handed slam.

The first-round pick had two points and three rebounds. After the game, Doncic made sure to grab the game ball as a memento for the rookie.

Review of Monetary Policy Strategy, Tools, and Communications

Mergers, Acquisitions, and Other Applications

Financial Stability Coordination & Actions

Financial Market Utilities & Infrastructures

For release at 2:30 p.m. EDT Share

The Federal Reserve Board on Thursday requested public comment on two proposals related to establishing a regulatory framework for Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.

The first proposal would require that Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers fully back their stablecoins with certain permissible reserve assets, such as short-term Treasury bills and certain other high-quality, liquid assets. The proposal would also establish standardized capital requirements to address certain credit and operational risks of payment stablecoin activities, as well as risk management standards, in accordance with the law. Separately, the proposal would introduce rules for Board-supervised firms that safekeep the assets backing payment stablecoins. It would also clarify the permissibility of stablecoin and related activities for Board-supervised banks.

The second proposal would establish a tailored application process for Board-supervised banks applying to issue payment stablecoins. These applicants would be required to submit a business plan and financial information, among other documents. The proposal would also create a process governing appeals, hearings, and final determinations for applications.

The comment period will close 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call (202) 452-2955.

Fans of the Kansas City Chiefs do not take the injury status of "day-to-day" at face value. It's been that way since safety Eric Berry held that status for what felt like the entire 2018 season.

So it's hard to take much away from head coach Andy Reid labeling three Chiefs players — quarterback Patrick Mahomes (elbow), wide receiver Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) — as "day-to-day" during his press conference on Monday. Still, it's an update.

Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here. For Android devices, click here.

Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury | ESPN

Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Monday that quarterback Patrick Mahomes is considered day-to-day with his right elbow injury, an injury he sustained in Sunday's win over the New York Jets. Reid shared that Mahomes was in the Chiefs' training facility Monday morning to receive treatment for his injury.

Following the game, an MRI scan didn't reveal any major injury to Mahomes' elbow, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

"It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick," Reid said Monday. "It looks like it's just a matter of [getting] some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We'll just see where it goes from there. He's in good spirits."

Former Chiefs player was roasted for his take on kicker Harrison Butker | The Kansas City Star

At 11:21 a.m. on Sunday, roughly 40 minutes before kickoff of the Jets game, ex-Chiefs wideout Gehrig Dieter shared this message on X: "I'm calling it now. Butker going to go on a generational run. He won't miss another kick the entire season."

Ninety minutes later, that generational run ended before it began as Butker missed a 51-yard attempt — after missing from 56 before a penalty gave him another shot. That led fans to believe his tenure with the Chiefs was nearly over, although coach Andy Reid said after the game he wasn't ready to announce a change.

Cover 32: What every team should do at NFL trade deadline, plus game balls and gaffes from Week 9 | CBS Sports

Kansas City Chiefs: Don't let the 35 points scored on Sunday fool you. The Chiefs still need wide receiver help, and not just a small addition either. They should be in on everyone from Brian Thomas Jr. to Josh Downs. I'd also go at the Jets hard with an offer for Garrett Wilson and make them say no. While a receiver is a clear need, I also think K.C. could stand to add a veteran edge rusher too.

'It feels like a matter of when' — NFL Insiders discuss Kansas City Chiefs' pursuit of WR Brian Thomas Jr. ahead of trade deadline | A to Z Sports

Jacksonville has a reason to listen. One factor that could make the Jaguars flinch and trade away a player like Thomas is the need to recoup draft capital, a point Fowler raised during the discussion.

ESPN's Adam Schefter outlined the compensation headed to the New Orleans Saints in the Jaguars' recent trade for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. The Saints are receiving a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick. However, that pick could turn into a 2027 sixth-round pick, depending on the conditions attached to the deal.

Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker reacts to getting booed off field: 'It is what it is' | Entertainment Weekly

"It's part of it, you know," he told reporters after the game. "I'm booing myself sometimes. People are passionate. Fans are passionate. They want to win games. They want me to make kicks. I want to make kicks. It's part of it. That's what you sign up for. I've got to do better."

The 10-year veteran is ranked the sixth-most-accurate kicker in NFL history, with an average of 87.1 percent of field goals made. But he's been struggling significantly this season and currently leads the league with seven missed field goals (over eight games).

NFL reinstates Brandon Aiyuk, gives 49ers 2-week roster exemption | The Athletic

The news comes three days after Aiyuk and his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, met with the 49ers' brass at the team's business offices in Santa Clara, Calif., with the receiver saying he was 100 percent healthy and seeking reinstatement. Aiyuk had been on the reserve/left squad list — where players are not paid and do not count against the team's roster numbers — since December and had not been to the team's facility since.

The 49ers have made it clear Aiyuk will never play for them again. Asked about the roster exemption Monday afternoon, coach Kyle Shanahan replied, "It means absolutely nothing to our team. … That's all administrative stuff to me."

Jaguars land DT Jordan Davis in blockbuster deal with Eagles, marking latest trade ahead of deadline | Yahoo! Sports

Jacksonville no longer has a first- or second-round draft pick in 2027 after Monday's transactions, though the Jaguars still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029.

The Jaguars have been to the playoffs only twice in the past nine seasons, and they fell in the wild-card round in 2025, the first under head coach Liam Coen's watch. While Monday's transactions were undoubtedly costly for the franchise, the Jaguars feel ready to go for it and make a legitimate postseason run. Whether that is enough for them to run the table in the AFC and make what would be the team's first Super Bowl remains to be seen.

Rams WR Puka Nacua likely to be placed on injured reserve with turf toe, sprained MCL and PCL | NFL.com

This marks the latest in a lengthy list of ailments for Nacua this season, as he was affected by psoas soreness throughout training camp and sat Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip injury, but the turf toe and knee sprain will lead to his longest absence yet.

Nacua is set to join fellow star wideout Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR, leaving the Rams with a WR corps of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and CJ Daniels, plus a tight end group of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen that is frequently used in the passing attack.

Chiefs Week 9 snap count analysis: Kristian Fulton steps up again

Since veteran slot cornerback L'Jarius Sneed was placed on the Reserve/Injured list before Week 8, the Chiefs have trusted safety Chris Roland-Wallace as the Nickel and primary slot defender.

With 45 snaps against New York, he out-snapped teammates in the secondary like safety Alohi Gilman (44 snaps) and safety Jaden Hicks (19 snaps). He has mainly been a staple in defending teams' quick passes, but he was also used on blitzes a season-high five times in Week 9; he registered two hurries.

#3027. Hornets humiliate the Cavs 124-112

The Cleveland Cavaliers, in desperate need of a get-right game, put together one of their worst performances in recent (regular season) memory by getting blown out by the Charlotte Hornets 124-112 on Monday night. The Cavs fall a game under .500 before heading to New York on Wednesday to play the defending champion Knicks on national television.

Instead of using tonight's game as a momentum builder, the Cavs were laughed out of the arena by the woeful Hornets. Cleveland trailed by as many as 33 points against the NBA's worst offense in Charlotte, a team that was already missing several key players. Grayson Allen (27 points on 8-of-14 shooting) and Naz Reid (25 points, 13 rebounds) thoroughly outplayed Cleveland's starters, resulting in a 16-point deficit at the half. That ballooned to 27 points at the end of the third quarter, leading to none of the Cavs' starters returning to the game after that.

Jarrett Allen returned to the starting lineup, finishing with 12 points and seven rebounds in 19 minutes. Donovan Mitchell and James Harden had 11 points each and combined to shoot 7-20 from the floor. Harden in particular was disastrous and had some of the worst defensive possessions you will ever see from an NBA player. Evan Mobley had an exceptionally ineffective game, too, with nine points and four turnovers. Harden and Mobley had a combined +/- of -46 tonight, which passes the eye test.

Not only did Charlotte's starters outplay the Cavs, but Cleveland's backups did too. Craig Porter Jr., Thomas Bryant, Thomas, and Norchad Omier brought the Cavs within eight points late in the fourth quarter before running out of steam. But the reserves showed a lot of heart, and considerably more effort and energy than Cleveland's starters.

The Cavs were out-rebounded 49-32 overall, but didn't get their first offensive rebound until the third quarter, losing that battle 17-3. Cleveland actually ended up with fewer turnovers and shot better from the field than Charlotte, but the final score didn't reflect that.

This is the type of loss that reverberates through an organization, especially one that is expensive and on a fixed timeline like the Cavs. There is a heightened sense of urgency to right the ship, but Cleveland remains exceptionally inconsistent and underwhelming. Despite quality wins against Minnesota and Philadelphia, the Cavs feel like a team teetering on the edge of the abyss. Losses like tonight's are what push things over.
